text:
Jean-Paul Laurent: Smoke test results for the updated quickstarts (agentic workflow template refresh) across Node/Python/Go. Ran from clean dirs w/ fresh deps.

Env used everywhere:
- `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=***`
- `export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwoodinference.com` (left default in Node + Py, set explicitly in Go)
- Model: `redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct` (tool calling), `redwood/llama-3.1-8b-instruct` (structured output retries)

Quick summary:
- Node (18.19): ✅ after 1 tiny fix (README + ESM import)
- Python (3.11): ✅ after pin/clarify `jsonschema` + a retry note
- Go (1.22): ⚠️ works, but example output in README was stale + one minor streaming loop footgun

Details below.

---
Node template (redwood-quickstarts `agentic-workflow-node`)
Command:
- `pnpm i && pnpm dev`
Observed:
- Streaming prints partial deltas OK
- Tool call invoked (`get_weather`) OK
- Structured output validation OK

Issue 1 (doc/ergonomics): README used `node index.js` but repo is TS + ESM; new users hit:
```
ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope
```
Fix: updated README to `pnpm dev` + explicit Node >=18 note.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts/pull/212 (already open, added small edit)

Issue 2 (small runtime): first run without `.env` printed a generic auth error.
Suggestion: print explicit "Missing REDWOOD_API_KEY" guard in the quickstart entrypoint.

---
Python template (redwood-quickstarts `agentic-workflow-python`)
Command:
- `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && python main.py`
Observed:
- Streaming OK
- Tool call args arrive in 2 chunks (partial JSON) but our assembly code handles it (👍 to the new loop)
- Structured output: 1/10 runs emitted trailing whitespace + newline before `}`; json parsing still OK; schema validation passes.

Issue: `jsonschema` wasn’t explicitly in requirements in one branch; people will copy/paste and then hit:
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jsonschema'`
Fix: add `jsonschema>=4.21` to requirements + a short note in README about retrying when schema validation fails.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts/pull/204 (needs small follow-up commit) 

---
Go template (redwood-quickstarts `agentic-workflow-go`)
Command:
- `go mod tidy && go run .`
Observed:
- Tool calling works
- Streaming loop works, but sample printed duplicate assistant content when a reconnect happened (I simulated by killing wifi for ~5s)

Repro notes:
- if you reconnect and re-consume the stream, you have to reset the incremental buffer OR de-dupe by event id.
- our sample currently appends deltas without guarding against a resumed stream.

Not a product bug, just example footgun. Suggestion: add a comment + minimal "if retry, start new request" guidance.

Also README expected output is from old tool-call shape (pre-parity). Needs update.

---
Action items:
1) @Dana Lo can you take the Node README tweak + missing key guard? (I can also do it if you’re slammed)
2) @Mateusz Zielinski can you update Go README expected output + add the retry caveat in the streaming loop?
3) @Sabrina James can you add `jsonschema` to the Py requirements and add the validation/retry snippet?

If folks are good w/ it, I’ll drop these into the launch checklist thread after PRs are merged.

Renee Sullivan: +1 on the explicit missing key guard. The #1 “quickstart broken” complaint from users is just “forgot to set env var” and we make it look scary. :facepalm:

Dana Lo: I can grab Node. The ESM thing is on me 😅
- I’ll update README to use `pnpm dev`
- add a preflight check for `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY`

Do we want to also print `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` if set (for people on VPC/private)?

Ibrahim Khan: +1 printing base URL when non-default. Keep it one line so it doesn’t clutter.

Sabrina James: I’ll take the Python requirements + retry note.
Also saw one run where structured output streamed an incomplete object until the final event; the example should emphasize “don’t parse until `response.completed` (or the final message)”.

Jean-Paul Laurent: Yep. That matches the new conventions doc. Add a comment like “accumulate chunks; parse at end; validate; if invalid, retry w/ stricter system msg”.

Mateusz Zielinski: On Go: I can patch today.
For the retry/disconnect behavior: I’d rather keep the sample simple and just say “don’t retry mid-stream; re-issue the request”. Implementing event-id de-dupe is a rabbit hole for a quickstart.

Sahana Iyer: Agree; keep quickstart simple.
If we want more robust retry logic, we can point to the `redwood-examples` repo and the golden fixtures once those land.

Wei Chen: For docs alignment: the Go README expected output should match the docs tool-call shape (tool name + arguments JSON + tool_result message). Please don’t show the old `function_call` key.

Mateusz Zielinski: yep, will update output snippet.

github-actions[bot]: PR #204 (agentic workflow template refresh) — checks: 
- lint: pass
- unit tests: pass
- smoke test: pending

Connor O'Brien: When you land these, please drop final PR links in #eng-releases thread so we can reference in the SDK versioning/changelog notes.

Dana Lo: I’ll push Node fixes to https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts/pull/212 in ~1h.

Sabrina James: I’ll add the python dependency + README note as a follow-up commit to #204.

Jean-Paul Laurent: Perfect. Once those are in, I’ll re-run the three smoke tests from scratch and reply here w/ final ✅ and the exact commit SHAs for the launch checklist.
